record.paper_title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems
record.context_brief: Dataset sufficiency for offline RL guarantees
record.original_question: In offline reinforcement learning, a learning algorithm receives only a fixed dataset D of transitions (state, action, next state, reward) collected by a behavior policy and cannot collect any additional environment interactions. What nontrivial, formally checkable sufficiency conditions on D guarantee that an offline reinforcement learning algorithm can recover an optimal or near-optimal policy, especially when high-reward regions of the state space may or may not be covered by the dataset?

evidence.quote: The offline reinforcement learning problem can be defined as a data-driven formulation of the reinforcement learning problem. The end goal is still to optimize the objective in Equation (1). However, the agent no longer has the ability to interact with the environment and collect additional transitions using the behavior policy. Instead, the learning algorithm is provided with a static dataset of transitions, D = {(sit, ait, sit+1, rit)}, and must learn the best policy it can using this dataset.

It is worth noting that defining this notion formally is itself an open problem, and to the best knowledge of the authors, there are no known non-trivial “sufficiency” conditions on D that allows us to formulate guarantees that any offline reinforcement learning algorithm will recover an optimal or near-optimal policy.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a Markov decision process M = (S, A, P, r, γ, ρ), where S is a (possibly infinite) state space, A an action space, P(s' | s, a) a transition kernel, r(s, a) ∈ [0, 1] a reward function, γ ∈ [0, 1) a discount factor, and ρ an initial state distribution. For a stationary policy π : S → Δ(A), define the value J(π) = E[Σ_{t≥0} γ^t r(s_t, a_t)] with s_0 ∼ ρ, a_t ∼ π(· | s_t), s_{t+1} ∼ P(· | s_t, a_t). An optimal policy π* satisfies J(π*) = sup_π J(π).

Offline data. A learner is given only a static dataset D = {(s_i, a_i, s'_i, r_i)}_{i=1}^N of transitions, drawn (i.i.d. or via a Markov chain) from the occupancy distribution induced by an unknown behavior policy π_β in M. The learner cannot interact further with M. An offline reinforcement learning algorithm is a (possibly randomized) map A : D ↦ π̂.

Problem. Identify a nontrivial, formally checkable sufficiency condition C(D) on the dataset D — a property whose validity can in principle be certified from D itself (and known properties of the function class used by the algorithm) without additional environment access — such that:

(i) C(D) does not require that D's induced state-action distribution covers the entire reachable state-action space (i.e., it must remain meaningful in regimes where high-reward regions of S may be poorly covered or even unvisited by π_β);

(ii) there exists an offline RL algorithm A and a function ε(N, C(D)) → 0 such that, whenever C(D) holds, the output π̂ = A(D) satisfies J(π*) − J(π̂) ≤ ε(N, C(D)) with high probability over the draw of D, uniformly over MDPs M consistent with C(D);

(iii) the condition C(D) is strictly weaker than the classical uniform concentrability/coverage condition that bounds sup_{s,a} d^{π*}(s, a) / d^{π_β}(s, a) by a finite constant.

Either exhibit such a condition C(D) together with the algorithm A and the bound ε, or prove that no such condition can exist for general offline RL.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent theoretical work has produced partial answers: under realizability and single-policy concentrability (coverage of only the optimal/comparator policy's occupancy), pessimistic algorithms (e.g., marginalized importance sampling with gap or density-ratio realizability) achieve PAC guarantees; bounded single-policy concentrability is known to be (essentially) necessary and sufficient in tabular and linear settings. However, fully checkable, distribution-free sufficiency conditions on D alone — without additional realizability/function-class assumptions — that strictly weaken uniform concentrability remain unresolved, so the question as originally posed is only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning with Realizability and Single-Policy Concentrability
status_evidence.snippet: Under a gap assumption, pessimistic algorithms based on marginalized importance sampling provide guarantees when the data covers the optimal policy and function classes realize the optimal value and density-ratio functions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides sufficiency results under single-policy coverage plus realizability, weakening uniform concentrability.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Single-Policy Sample Complexity and Transient Coverage for Average-Reward Offline RL
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp guarantees depending only on the target policy via bias span and a policy hitting radius, giving the first fully single-policy sample complexity bound for average-reward offline RL.
status_evidence.claim: Recent refinements give target-policy-only coverage conditions sufficient for near-optimality.

status_evidence.title: A Tutorial: An Intuitive Explanation of Offline Reinforcement Learning Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Bounded concentrability coefficient C* is a necessary and sufficient condition to obtain a near-optimal policy using offline data.
status_evidence.claim: Concentrability-based conditions are known sufficiency conditions, but formally checkable from D alone is not established.
